Depth of reported AI involvement

The report assigns each disclosure of AI use to one category based on the strongest role described. Select a bar to browse the papers.

Extensive generation can refer to a core result, most proofs, or a substantial manuscript draft. AI workflows

Manuscript claims. Independent review is outside this report’s scope.

Depth definitions

CategoryEvidence used for classification
Editing onlyThe described role is copyediting, formatting, or improving presentation.
Support and checkingThe described role includes lookup or error checking, sometimes with editing.
Research contributionThe statement describes exploration, calculations, coding, technical help, or drafting assistance without attributing a specific finished contribution.
Substantive generationThe statement credits AI with producing a specific proof, result, construction, or substantial manuscript section.
Extensive generationThe statement credits AI with a core result, most proofs, or a full or broad manuscript draft.
Scope unspecifiedThe statement reports use with insufficient detail to assign another category.

Shared research problems

These submissions explicitly study the same core problem. Each row shows the method and the paper’s AI disclosure status.

Fixed-parameter algorithms for 4-block integer programming

Both papers give a fixed-parameter algorithm for general 4-block integer linear programs and describe the other as concurrent work. They use the same broad convex-extensibility framework. Their submitted versions also treat separable convex objectives.

2 of 2 report AI use.

SubmissionMethodAI disclosure
#350 · A Fixed-Parameter Algorithm for 4-Block Integer Programming (31 pages) PDF p. 8Uses conformal bisection on the local variables and residuals to prove midpoint convexity on residue classes, then refines the classes so the global value function can be optimized separately on each.AI use disclosed #350 PDF p. 17
#392 · 4-Block Integer Programming is in FPT (21 pages) PDF p. 3Proves a general lemma making integer-midpoint-convex functions convex extensible on sufficiently dilated low-dimensional lattices, then applies it to block-structured value functions.AI use disclosed #392 PDF p. 12

Almost-linear algorithms for Subset Sum

Both papers report the same one-dimensional result. They share a convex-geometric covering theorem and Macbeath regions. The recursive paper also handles multidimensional inputs.

2 of 2 report AI use.

SubmissionMethodAI disclosure
#29 · Subset Sum in Almost-Linear Time (83 pages) PDF p. 5Partitions the input items into groups, computes group-level representations of attainable sums, and merges them from the bottom up.AI use disclosed #29 PDF p. 16
#1536 · An Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Multidimensional Subset Sum (63 pages) PDF p. 8Recurses on smaller instances by covering boundary targets with parallelepipeds and reducing interior targets separately. The recursion also supports multidimensional Subset Sum.AI use disclosed #1536 PDF p. 6

Approximate counting in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model

Both papers report deterministic polynomial-time approximation of the SK partition function for 0 ≤ β < 1, with high probability over the disorder. Both use graph expansions and color coding. Their higher-order results have different scopes.

2 of 2 report AI use.

SubmissionMethodAI disclosure
#592 · Color coding for the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model (33 pages) PDF p. 5Extends color coding for graph expansions to mixtures with both quadratic and higher-order interactions.AI use disclosed
#1559 · Polynomial-time algorithms for mean-field models up to the glass transition (180 pages) PDF p. 71Evaluates retained graph terms by color-subset dynamic programming and removes the coloring restriction with a deterministic average.AI use disclosed #1559 PDF p. 73

Three submissions on the Matrix Spencer conjecture

All three papers report the conjectured order of discrepancy for the square case. Two use hereditary Gaussian small-ball estimates; the third uses a different potential. Constants and algorithmic guarantees differ.

3 of 3 report AI use.

SubmissionMethodAI disclosure
#165 · Matrix Spencer: Eight Standard Deviations Suffice and an Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Dense Input (314 pages) PDF p. 1Turns hereditary Gaussian small-ball bounds into partial signings through concentration, projection, or a counting argument. A separate projection-based algorithm gives an almost-linear running time in the dense input size.AI use disclosed #165 PDF p. 310
#619 · A Walk from Free Probability to Matrix Discrepancy I: Matrix Spencer (94 pages) PDF p. 1Runs a random walk whose potential tracks a smoothed spectral edge of a free-probability model of the remaining randomness.AI use disclosed #619 PDF p. 66
#1742 · A Proof of the Matrix Spencer Conjecture (37 pages) PDF p. 3Uses a determinantal weight to obtain a hereditary Gaussian small-ball bound, then repeatedly applies Gluskin’s partial-coloring method.AI use disclosed #1742 PDF p. 34

Impossibility results

NP-completeness

Huffman coding with unequal costs

Scope
The two letter costs are consecutive positive integers supplied as part of the input.
Result
Deciding whether a binary prefix code meets a given cost threshold is NP-complete.

Theorem 1.1 · PDF p. 5 · #1394 · Binary Huffman Coding with Unequal Letter Costs Is NP-Complete (51 pages)

Conditional hardness

Approximating MAX-3-CUT

Scope
Assume the Unique Games Conjecture.
Result
Achieving an approximation ratio of α₃ + ε is NP-hard for every ε > 0, where α₃ ≈ 0.836008.

Theorem 1.4 · PDF p. 4 · #1269 · Sharp Hardness for MAX-3-CUT and Quantum MAX-CUT (46 pages)

Oracle separation

Relativized quantum verification

Scope
Both complexity classes have access to the same classical oracle.
Result
There is an oracle relative to which BQP is not contained in IP.

Corollary 6.8 · PDF p. 22 · #156 · BQP⊆IP Does Not Relativize (31 pages)

Information limit

Posted prices under moment ambiguity

Scope
The seller knows every exact moment of the buyer’s value distribution and may randomize the posted price.
Result
For any such rule, worst-case revenue can be arbitrarily small compared with the best posted-price revenue when the distribution is known.

Theorem 5.2 · PDF p. 13 · #44 · Moment Ambiguity and the Limits of Robust Stochastic Optimization (38 pages)

Information limit

Secretary selection under moment ambiguity

Scope
Labeled values arrive in random order. Their magnitudes are observed, and all distribution moments are disclosed. The bound holds even for i.i.d. values.
Result
The optimal worst-case success probability equals the classical secretary value at every horizon and tends to 1/e.

Theorem 6.1 · PDF p. 16 · #44 · Moment Ambiguity and the Limits of Robust Stochastic Optimization (38 pages)

Corollary 6.2 · PDF p. 17 · #44

Round lower bound

Distributed maximal independent set

Scope
A randomized LOCAL algorithm must succeed with a fixed positive probability on every n-vertex graph.
Result
The worst-case round count is Ω(log n / log log n).

Theorem 1.1 · PDF p. 3 · #411 · No Truly Sublogarithmic-Round Algorithm for Distributed MIS in the LOCAL Model (35 pages)

Variance lower bound

Private continual counting

Scope
Bounded-sensitivity Gaussian factorization counters are time-invariant or have a fixed period.
Result
The prefix variance divided by (ln t)² diverges as t grows.

Theorem 1.1(i) · PDF p. 3 · #86 · Sharp Limits of Time Invariance in Private Continual Counting (32 pages)

Nonexistence

Fair division with submodular values

Scope
Three agents have weighted-coverage valuations over eight indivisible goods.
Result
Some such instances admit no complete allocation that is envy-free up to any good (EFX).

Theorem 1.1 · PDF p. 2 · #1295 · Counterexamples to EFX for Submodular and Subadditive Valuations (67 pages)

Circuit lower bound

Computing majority with shallow circuits

Scope
Depth-three OR–AND–OR circuits have bottom fan-in at most three.
Result
The output gate needs exponentially many inputs to compute majority on n bits.

Corollary 1.5 · PDF p. 4 · #677 · The Exact Complexity of Majority in Depth-Three Circuits with Bottom Fan-in Three (30 pages)

Quantum communication lower bound

Multiple Hidden Matching

Scope
The input string is uniform. The m requests are independent draws from a balanced distribution on perfect matchings of [N], with m ≤ N^(1/2−δ) and fixed δ, ε ∈ (0, 1/2).
Result
Any one-way protocol answering every request correctly with probability at least 1−ε must send Ω(m) qubits.

Theorem 6.7 · PDF p. 30 · #1371 · Four Ways to Stream: Exponential Separations from Random Order and Quantum Memory (51 pages)

AI workflows

Two independent results on 4-block integer programming

The teams describe their fixed-parameter algorithms as independent and concurrent. One credits GPT-6 Astra with finding the final proof. The other credits GPT-6 Astra Pro with help developing and proving specific lemmas and a proposition, and names additional assistance for an appendix.

#350 · A Fixed-Parameter Algorithm for 4-Block Integer Programming (31 pages) PDF p. 17 · #392 · 4-Block Integer Programming is in FPT (21 pages) PDF p. 12

AI as a subject and a tool

10 papers were tagged as studying generative AI or LLMs. 6 of those also disclosed AI assistance. Submission #9 illustrates the distinction in a single paper.

#9 · Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution (32 pages) PDF p. 32

From checking to proof development

Submission #2 reports using AI to check and choose among proof options the authors had developed. Submission #11 reports AI-assisted proof drafting and a simplification that strengthened several lower bounds.

#2 · Potential Hessian Ascent IV: Sampling the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model at Beta < 1 (52 pages) PDF p. 44 · #11 · The universal measure of nonstochastic objects (32 pages) PDF p. 4 · #11 PDF p. 15

A statement can report minor editing

Submission #12 reports proofreading and minor edits. The CFP exempts minor copyediting from mandatory disclosure, so this is an example of disclosure beyond the minimum policy.

#12 · The power of time reversal in Hamiltonian property testing (37 pages) PDF p. 25

A timeline from prompts to an algorithm

The Matrix Spencer submission dates its first prompts to July 28, a first proof to August 20, and an SDP algorithm to August 25. It credits AI chiefly for the existence argument and attributes most constant improvements and the core algorithmic ideas to the authors.

#165 · Matrix Spencer: Eight Standard Deviations Suffice and an Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Dense Input (314 pages) PDF p. 309

Using different tools at different stages

The Most Informative Boolean Function submission describes using models for finding counterexamples, testing inequalities, implementing interval arithmetic, critiquing proofs, and assisting with Lean. The authors credit themselves with the Bellman framework and final proof strategy.

#527 · A Proof of the Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture (276 pages) PDF p. 274

Stronger bounds left out of the manuscript

The authors say agents suggested slightly stronger bounds for a multi-item auction problem. They omitted those analyses because they found them opaque, numerically complex, and short on additional insight.

#1053 · On the Power of Determinism in Multi-Item Auctions (68 pages) PDF p. 64

A first draft and proofs of most results

After five years of preliminary research, the authors supplied their results and steered an iterative investigation. They credit GPT-6 Astra with an initial manuscript and proofs of most results, then describe rewriting the drafts themselves.

#7 · A Constant-Factor Approximation to Multidimensional Consumer Utility (61 pages) PDF p. 28

A Gemini-based harness obtained the main result

The authors say the Cogentic framework obtained the main result using an internal Gemini model. They report providing the problem, verifying the proofs and contextualizing the findings.

#1151 · The Power of Recruiting the Smaller Side: Two Additional Traders Suffice in Two-Sided Markets (40 pages) PDF p. 1

The authors proposed a witness-encryption strategy. They say Codex with ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra identified the bounded-factor MinRank variant and supplied major proof ideas and an initial draft.

The author says most proofs were drafted using AI tools. A simplification found with AI assistance strengthened multiple lower bounds. The author reports checking the proofs.

#1558 · Supply-Sensitive Revenue Recovery under Unknown Buyer Order (20 pages) · #1560 · Optimal Law-Local Compression for Stochastic Loads (22 pages) · #1566 · Stochastic Load Balancing with Strict Machine-Reservation Budgets (14 pages) · #1568 · Online Average-Value Allocation: A Sharp Information Frontier (17 pages) · #1573 · Nearly Exact Length Bounds for Directed Steiner Tree and Forest in Planar Graphs (19 pages)

Three submissions on Matrix Spencer

Song and Zhang report existence with a discrepancy constant below eight and an almost-linear randomized algorithm in the size of dense input for a below-12 guarantee. They cite separate resolutions by Akbas and Sra via a hereditary small-ball estimate and by Kathuria via a random walk guided by free probability.

#165 · Matrix Spencer: Eight Standard Deviations Suffice and an Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Dense Input (314 pages) · #619 · A Walk from Free Probability to Matrix Discrepancy I: Matrix Spencer (94 pages) · #1742 · A Proof of the Matrix Spencer Conjecture (37 pages)

Two submissions on almost-linear Subset Sum

Jin and Mao say Chen, Mao, and Zhang independently obtained their one-dimensional result. Both approaches use Macbeath regions and the same convex-geometric covering theorem. The former combines groups of items from the bottom up, while the latter uses a top-down recursion and extends the result to multiple dimensions.

#29 · Subset Sum in Almost-Linear Time (83 pages) · #1536 · An Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Multidimensional Subset Sum (63 pages)

Two counting algorithms below the spin-glass transition

The color-coding paper credits Schmidhuber and Zlokapa with an independent deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for approximating the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick partition function below the critical inverse temperature. It also extends the color-coding argument to mixtures containing both quadratic and higher-order interactions.

#592 · Color coding for the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model (33 pages) · #1559 · Polynomial-time algorithms for mean-field models up to the glass transition (180 pages)

Half the gains from trade

One team pins down the worst-case efficiency of second-best bilateral trade at one half. A second gives a mechanism guaranteeing at least half of first-best gains in multidimensional, two-sided markets with additive values and costs and downward-closed feasibility constraints, and cites the bilateral paper for tightness.

#353 · Second-Best Bilateral Trade is $1/2$ Efficient (65 pages) · #529 · Second-Best Trade Is Half Efficient in Multidimensional Markets (29 pages)

Two barriers for envy-free allocation

One paper gives a three-agent, eight-good instance with no allocation that is envy-free up to any good, even for submodular valuations. Another shows that with strictly positive additive valuations, envy-freeness up to any good can conflict with Pareto optimality.

#1295 · Counterexamples to EFX for Submodular and Subadditive Valuations (67 pages) · #296 · Pareto Inefficiency of EFX (15 pages)

Corpus and links

The report includes the current public index and retains one submission from the original snapshot. The manifest records PDF page counts and checksums. Evidence links use PDF page numbers.

Names and graph

Author counts use the names listed in the index. Different people can share a name, and one person can appear under different spellings. Each coauthor pair counts once per paper. Recurring teams are matched by their full author lists, regardless of order.

Affiliations

Affiliations are taken from the submissions and grouped by institution and location.

Topics

Topic labels use titles and available abstracts or opening text. A paper can have a primary topic and secondary tags. Papers with too little evidence remain unclassified. The catalog shows the text basis and matched terms.

AI evidence

We identify AI use from authors’ disclosures in the PDFs. A missing or unclear statement leaves AI use uncertain. A paper can have several purpose or tool tags, and depth reflects the strongest role the authors report. Group-level disclosure shares use papers with readable text.

Interpretation

The figures describe the public submissions at the snapshot date. Topic labels and AI-use categories depend on the available text. Differences across groups are descriptive, and research claims come from the manuscripts.

AI policy

The call for papers requires disclosure when generative AI materially affects substantive content. Minor copyediting is exempt. Official CFP

Formalization and repositories

We count authors’ reports of Lean or Rocq use, including partial formalizations. A public source counts when the code is accessible and tied to the paper. Independent verification and SAT or SMT checks are listed separately. Lean documentation

AI analysis guide

Copy the prompt into your AI assistant to ask questions about the report or explore a new analysis.

Prompt for an analysis agent

First ask me what I want to learn from the STOC 2027 submissions. Use the report and repository to answer my question. State the denominator, report missing data, and link to the original PDFs.

If a code change would help, shallow-clone the repository and download only the PDF snapshots needed for the analysis. Suggest a small pull request with a reproducible check.

Report website https://conference-stats.github.io/stoc-2027/stats.html

GitHub repository https://github.com/conference-stats/stoc-2027

Example questions
